rules: library-literal matches an ordinal substring of each decoded string-literal use across the selected implementation libraries. Preserve operand whitespace, newlines, case, and all other text; do not normalize. The operand is 1..1024 UTF-16 code units. Repeated identical operands collapse, while distinct operands are incompatible.

The empty library-literal values list is not an allow list: any decoded UTF-16 text satisfying its constraints is accepted. An operand of 600 astral Unicode characters is 1200 UTF-16 code units and is rejected by the 1024-unit maximum.

library-literal and --tfm require each other. Supply library-target as one exact NuGet TFM through --tfm, while dependency-target is a --where term. Literal inspection downloads package content; dependency predicates use nuspec data.

Without dependency-depth, exact depends matches direct dependencies. With depth 2, 3, or 4 it matches direct or transitive declaration paths up to that maximum. The preferred new syntax is exact depends plus dependency-depth; legacy depends-transitive matches only paths of depth 2 through the maximum, so a direct-only hit does not satisfy it. A starts-with depends predicate remains direct and cannot alone admit depth.

dependency-depth accepts exactly 2, 3, or 4, so depth 1 is illegal. Traversal requires an explicit dependency-target TFM and an exact depends or legacy depends-transitive predicate; dependency-target=all is illegal for the second command. The depth is a maximum declaration-edge depth, not a row limit. Repeated exact depends terms are ANDed and share traversal.

At most five package candidates may be admitted for these inspection predicates; an exact package ID admits one. For Microsoft.Azure.* set --take 5 explicitly to bound candidate work and -n 2 to bound final returned rows. The final-row limit does not substitute for the candidate-work bound.
